title: Two-copy distillability of one-copy-undistillable negative-partial-transpose states in every dimension
authors: Gelo Noel M. Tabia, Kai-Siang Chen, Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract: Whether negative-partial-transpose (NPT) states that are undistillable from one copy become distillable from finitely many copies remains a basic open problem in entanglement theory. We study the canonical two-parameter family of DiVincenzo \textit{et al.}, introduced as a symmetry-reduced testbed for this question. We prove that a distinguished one-copy-undistillable state in this family is already two-copy distillable in every local dimension $d\geq 3$. A uniform equal-norm tight-frame construction gives explicit Schmidt-rank-two certificates in every dimension, thereby disproving the conjecture that the entire one-copy-undistillable region of the canonical family remains undistillable for arbitrarily many copies. The same witnesses certify an open two-copy-distillable neighborhood around the counterexample, while separately constructed three-copy witnesses enlarge the inner bounds for the distillable region in the surrounding parameter space. In contrast, recent results for Werner states, together with the propagation argument of DiVincenzo \textit{et al.}, establish a neighboring region of one-copy-undistillable states that remains two-copy undistillable. Thus a single symmetry-reduced family contains rigorously certified states with opposite two-copy behavior, separated by a substantial region whose finite-copy distillability remains unresolved.
summary: The paper investigates the distillability of negative-partial-transpose quantum states by testing if one-copy-undistillable states become distillable with multiple copies. Using fixed witnesses and tensor product constructions, the authors prove that a specific state family is two-copy distillable for all dimensions $d \geq 3$. This result significantly refines our understanding of entanglement boundaries in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The central problem is determining if negative-partial-transpose (NPT) states, which are undistillable from a single copy, become distillable when multiple copies are available.
main_result: The authors prove that a specific one-copy-undistillable state within the canonical family is two-copy distillable in every dimension $d \geq 3$, contradicting previous conjectures about its persistence of undistillability.
method: The study employs constructing fixed quantum witnesses (e.g., $|\Psi_dangle$) whose expectation values are calculated on tensor products of the state to test for negative entanglement measures indicative of distillability.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on bipartite quantum states $ho$ exhibiting NPT, specifically utilizing a canonical two-parameter family introduced by DiVincenzo et al. The results hold for arbitrary local dimensions $d \geq 3$.
key_observables: Distillability status (one-copy vs. two-copy), and the sign of expectation values calculated using fixed witnesses.
important_parameters: The local dimension $d$, and the state parameters $(b, c)$ defining the canonical family $ho_{b,c}$.
main_assumptions: The derived bounds are based on analytic fixed witnesses and do not necessarily represent the fully optimized distillability boundaries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the parameter plane for NPT states in $d=3$, showing regions certified as two-copy distillable (blue lobe) versus those whose status is unresolved, comparing results from two-copy vs. three-copy witnesses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the distillability of canonical NPT states by first establishing a two-copy witness for general $d \geq 3$, then constructing and analyzing stronger three-copy witnesses, and finally mapping out the resulting certified regions on the parameter plane.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical proofs regarding entanglement properties (distillability) in structured quantum states, which is foundational knowledge for understanding resource theories in quantum information processing.
